title: `model_registry.py validate` decides promotion by comparing criteria recorded on different snapshot dates — the exact unpaired comparison promotion.py's docstring says invalidates the verdict
claimUnderTest: promotion.py module docstring: 'the comparison is always made on ONE snapshot with both curves scored against it… A rule that compared this week's challenger to last week's champion SCORE would be reading five days of market drift as model quality.'
observed: cmd_validate reads champ.holdout['criterion'] and challenger.holdout['criterion'] straight out of the registry JSON and feeds both to decide_promotion. Those two numbers were recorded on different days against different scrapes of the four holdout CSVs. Champion v2's criterion is stamped 2026-07-28; challenger v3's is stamped 2026-08-04. Running `validate 3` today prints improvement +12.8; the paired comparison of the same two parameter sets on today's boards is +22.3, and the registry's own v3 note (written by the PAIRED driver) records +22.4. The CLI is off by 9.6 points against a 25-point margin whose stated noise floor is ~1.5 points.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python scripts/model_registry.py validate 3 && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.model_registry.holdout import evaluate_offense_master as e;a=e(0.11,1.11).criterion;b=e(0.108,1.11).criterion;print('paired improvement today: %+.2f' % (a-b))"
reproduction.expected: the CLI's improvement equals the paired improvement
reproduction.actual: CLI: 'improvement +12.8 does not clear the 25-point margin'; paired today: +22.25

userImpact: No user-visible number today — both paths reject v3. But the operator-facing decision tool disagrees with the automated driver by 6.3x the noise the margin was sized against, so it can reject a genuine improvement or promote a non-improvement, and the operator has no signal that the two disagree. `status` compounds it by printing three criteria from three dates in one comparable-looking column.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced by running the CLI and the paired evaluation side by side; the prior finding asserts the defect but not the 9.5-point live magnitude.

whatWorks: auto_refit_hill_curves.py, the automated path, DOES score both curves on one snapshot and is correct. promotion.decide_promotion itself is a clean, well-documented function.
rootCause: decide_promotion takes two scalars and cannot tell whether they came from one snapshot; the CLI is the caller that supplies mismatched ones.
requiredRepair: cmd_validate must re-score the champion's params via evaluate_offense_master before comparing, exactly as the driver does. Stored per-version criteria should be labelled with the snapshot fingerprint they were measured on and never compared across rows.
